Narrow the kebab arm to require evidence that a token was ever a skill. Ordering in workLog is sequential; timestamps mark order only, not measured wall-clock times.

workLog.action: Reproduced the issue against the real corpus
workLog.detail: Scanning .serena/memories produced 210 findings: 183 skill_name across 122 distinct tokens, plus 27 script_path. Intersecting those 122 tokens with the 8 genuinely deleted skills returned the empty set, confirming the issue's claim of 0 true positives. A planted reference to a deleted skill did produce a finding, proving the detector was live and not simply misconfigured.

workLog.action: Refuted the issue's own suggested fix with measurement
workLog.detail: The issue proposes detecting only typed references. Classifying all 1790 repo-wide skill_name findings gave 68 true positives, of which only 11 are typed. Typed-only would discard 57 true positives, 21 of them on live surfaces including six inside .claude/skills/doc-accuracy/SKILL.md.
workLog.outcome: Typed-only rejected on evidence; recorded in the code comment so it is not retried.

workLog.action: Chose the union rule and verified it against precedent
workLog.detail: A token is a candidate when it is typed as a skill OR appears in a curated set of names that were once skills. The repo already ships this exact shape for single-word tokens (KNOWN_SINGLE_WORD_SKILLS, added by #2679 for the identical false-positive-flood reason), so the fix is existing precedent applied to the kebab arm rather than a new mechanism.
workLog.outcome: Predicted 90 repo-wide findings with all 68 true positives retained.

workLog.action: Rejected git history as the runtime evidence source
workLog.detail: Deriving 'was ever a skill' from git log at scan time would silently return nothing under actions/checkout's default depth of 1, making the arm inert in CI without failing. A curated frozenset is deterministic in shallow clones and vendored installs. A drift test derives the same set from history and skips when git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository is not false.
workLog.outcome: Curated set with a history-derived drift guard.

workLog.action: Implemented and re-measured against the running code
workLog.detail: Repo-wide batched scan over 3433 tracked markdown files reported exactly 90 skill_name findings, down from 1790, retaining all 68 true positives. .serena/memories went from 183 to 1. The single residual finding is a typed reference to land-and-deploy, a gstack skill this repo never shipped; it is pinned by name in a test rather than suppressed, because it is a correct finding.

Restoring the old open premise in scan.py failed 27 tests, all of them the new noise and corpus assertions. Separately emptying KNOWN_KEBAB_SKILLS failed 7 tests, all of them the retired-name detection and drift assertions. The two failure sets do not overlap, so each half of the rule is independently load-bearing. Both files restored; 191 tests pass.
workLog.outcome: Both halves proven necessary, not just jointly sufficient.

workLog.action: Retyped 29 fixture references rather than weaken assertions
workLog.detail: 17 pre-existing tests failed after the change because their fixtures wrote bare backticked names. Each was rewritten to the typed form so the fixture still expresses a skill reference. Diffing the two premise-testing tests before and after confirmed each test's actual subject (exit codes, truncation, baseline suppression, glob expansion) was unchanged.
workLog.outcome: Faithful re-expression, not a lowered bar.

workLog.action: Measured KEBAB_DENYLIST and left it alone deliberately
workLog.detail: Emptying the entire ~90-entry KEBAB_DENYLIST changes nothing repo-wide: still exactly 90 findings, zero new tokens surfaced. It is now provably dead. Deleting it is a separate behavior change and was filed as its own issue so each change keeps an independent revert point.
workLog.outcome: Measured, reported, and scoped out on purpose.

workLog.action: Fixed vendor-portability drift the pre-push hook caught
workLog.detail: The first push was rejected: check_skill_portability reported 17 upstream-path refs in the test file against a baseline of 11. The new tests had hard-coded .claude/skills and counted parents[4] to reach the repository root. Both are wrong in the generated mirror, which sits at a different depth. Replaced with a catalog resolved from the test's own location (parents[2] is the catalog in both trees), a repository root found by walking up to .git, and a fixture catalog located by shape. Refs returned to 11 and the check exits 0.
workLog.outcome: No drift, and the new tests now work from the vendored copy too.

workLog.action: Scoped the drift guard to the canonical catalog after the mirror run failed
workLog.detail: Running the mirrored copy failed the drift guard because the mirror's deletion history lists merge-resolver, which is live canonically. That exposed a separate defect: merge-resolver exists in .claude/skills but is absent from the generated src/copilot-cli/skills catalog, while AGENTS.md routes conflict resolution to it. Filed separately. The guard now skips in the mirror, since generated deletions are generation events rather than retirements, and the curated set describes retirements.
workLog.outcome: Canonical 191 pass, mirror 190 pass 1 skip, both together 381 pass with no module-key collision.

workLog.action: Dropped the ScanResult annotation on the _skill_names test helper
workLog.evidence: git_hook_policy.py mypy is a changed-line ratchet (issue #2993); it blocked on test_scan.py:1855 valid-type and :1856 attr-defined because ScanResult is a runtime alias of a dynamically loaded module, not a static type. No other use in the file annotates with it. After the edit the ratchet exits 0 and ruff passes on the file.
